question: Immediately after delivery, you apply the NRP initial assessment. Which THREE questions determine whether a newborn can remain with the mother or requires resuscitation?

answers.text: Term gestation? Clear amniotic fluid? Breathing or crying? Good muscle tone?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. These are the four NRP 2020 rapid assessment questions. If ALL four are YES — term, clear fluid, breathing/crying, good tone — the baby stays with the mother for routine care. Any NO triggers resuscitation steps.

answers.text: APGAR ≥7? No meconium? Skin-to-skin in place? Cord clamped?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: APGAR scoring takes 1 full minute and is NOT the initial assessment tool. The NRP initial questions are assessed in the first 30 seconds before any APGAR score can be calculated.

answers.text: Heart rate >100 bpm? Respiratory rate >30/min? SpO₂ >90%? Temperature >36.5°C?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: These vital sign thresholds are not the NRP pre-resuscitation checklist. Pulse oximetry and temperature measurement come later in the NRP algorithm, not as initial triage questions.

answers.text: Singleton? Vaginal delivery? No maternal fever? Cord pH obtained?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Mode of delivery, singleton status, and cord pH are relevant background context but are NOT the four NRP initial assessment questions that guide the immediate resuscitation decision.

overallFeedback.feedback: Memorise the NRP 4 initial questions: term gestation? clear amniotic fluid? breathing or crying? good muscle tone? Any NO triggers the resuscitation sequence.
Correct. The NRP 4-question initial assessment (term? clear fluid? tone? breathing?) takes under 30 seconds and determines the entire initial resuscitation pathway.
